Ahn Hyo-seop’s First Chef Role Is Streaming in Singapore on Prime Video
 The DANAMIC Team November 1, 2026 4 minutes read

 Final Table has been streaming exclusively on Prime Video in Singapore since Saturday, 24 October 2026 . It premiered the same day in more than 240 other countries and territories. Prime Video is included with an Amazon Prime membership, and members can share it through Amazon Family, so the whole household can follow this one.
 The Korean drama stars Ahn Hyo-seop in his first chef role, a turn Prime Video first announced in September . It’s a scripted culinary survival drama, so the contest at its centre, “The Table: K-Chef 2026” , is fiction, though the cast say the knife work took real training. For anyone who watches cooking shows for the plating shots, Final Table is the one to start with.
 Meet the Chefs at the Table
 The story follows Korean chefs from around the world as they compete to be crowned the finest Korean chef. Ahn, known for Business Proposal , Dr. Romantic and KPop Demon Hunters , plays Kang Han, a world-class chef who goes by Chris K. Hong Hwa-yeon plays Choi Song-yi, who is fighting to save her late father’s restaurant, Famiglia. Chang Ryul is Cha Woo-jin, a perfectionist star chef determined to reclaim his pride, while Jung Eu-gene plays Seon Jeong-won, an executive producer at Pyeongyeon Media.
 A chef in a white jacket and a Famiglia apron stands in the kitchen of the restaurant at the heart of Song-yi’s story As the competition heats up, their personal stories tangle and the rivalries turn into unexpected connections. Each chef wants the trophy for a different reason, whether that’s pride, a family restaurant or something Kang Han keeps to himself. Those stakes give every cooking scene more weight than a judge’s verdict ever could.
 Two Months of Morning Lessons
 Ahn worked on everything from knife skills and wok techniques to plating, which is arranging a dish the way a restaurant would serve it. “Since I was playing a professional, I didn’t want there to be any flaws,” he said at the press conference. He studied the composure, expressions and movements of real chefs on cooking competition shows. “What impressed me most was how calm they remained,” he explained, and that calm suits a character whose cooking is all precision.
 A chef in a white double-breasted jacket leans over a steel counter in a scene from Final Table According to Prime Video, Chang took two-hour cooking lessons every morning for nearly two months . “I realized just how difficult it was to handle professional cooking tools,” he said, adding that he grew most confident at preparing ingredients.
 Writer-director Kim Doh-hoon said the cast’s preparation was so thorough that professional cooking doubles were hardly needed. That’s the production’s own claim, and the kitchen scenes are where viewers can test it for themselves.
 Final Table’s kitchen scenes are where you can judge the cast’s cooking skills for yourself Rivals on Screen, Friends Off It
 Woo-jin and Kang Han are fierce rivals, yet Chang and Ahn became close friends on set. Ahn admitted that the friendship had him wondering how they would pull off the rivalry at all. “But the moment the cameras started rolling, his eyes completely changed,” he said, which is promising news for anyone who watches K-dramas for the stare-downs.
 Two Final Table cast members in dark suits shake hands at the press conference, all smiles for a show built on kitchen rivalries Jung was drawn to how vividly the script writes everyone around the main trio. “Every character felt alive, and I found it fascinating how each person had a different way of living,” she said. A strong ensemble matters in a competition story, since the chefs knocked out early need to be worth missing!
 A Restaurant Worth Saving
 Hong has played a chef before, and that history is exactly why Song-yi appealed to her. “In my previous culinary drama, my character was already a chef, but this time, I was drawn to the fact that Song-yi has room to grow,” she explained. She wanted to bring out the character’s kindness, diligence and strong sense of justice.
 Hong Hwa-yeon, who plays Song-yi, waves at the Final Table press conference Asked to sum up the series as a flavour, Hong picked salty , because Song-yi’s heartbreaking start eventually gives way to moving moments and tears. It’s an honest choice for a show selling healing, and it tells viewers to keep tissues within reach.
 The Director’s Food Obsession
 Kim, best known for Moon Embracing the Sun , wrote and directed Final Table after exploring the culinary world since 2014. “Every line of dialogue and every scene description required an understanding of cooking, which made the writing process particularly challenging,” he said. He called the series a bold creative experiment and expects viewers to wonder whether they’re watching a variety show (Korea’s term for unscripted entertainment) or a drama.
 Ahn Hyo-seop, who plays world-class chef Kang Han, waves at the Final Table press conference in a black oversized suit He pushed the actors to meet professional chefs and understand their mindset. “I believe that the more time actors spend thinking like the people they portray, the more naturally they become those characters,” he said. Kim wanted to capture the identity of Korean cuisine through chefs with global experience, and he would rather start conversations about food and culture than hand out definitive answers. For a show about crowning the “finest Korean chef”, that’s a thoughtful twist.
 Why It’s Worth Your Weekend
 The cast kept circling back to the same idea at the press conference. “What moved me was that the story goes beyond competition to explore family and love,” Chang said. Ahn praised how the script explores people and relationships, while Hong hoped viewers would feel its warmth and watch with family and friends.
 The Final Table cast pose and wave in front of the series backdrop at the production press conference Kim compared the series to a meal, describing it as a fresh take on the familiar world of cooking. The pick here is the Ahn and Chang rivalry, two actors who trained for weeks to look at home behind a pass, with Song-yi’s fight for Famiglia as the emotional anchor. Fans of Business Proposal who want to see Ahn play someone sharper and more guarded have their weekend sorted. 
 🗓️ Premiered: Saturday, 24 October 2026
📍 Where to watch: Exclusively on Prime Video, in Singapore and more than 240 countries and territories
🎬 Starring: Ahn Hyo-seop, Hong Hwa-yeon, Chang Ryul and Jung Eu-gene
🎥 Writer and director: Kim Doh-hoon
🍳 The contest: “The Table: K-Chef 2026”, the fictional competition at the heart of the story
 Photos and Visuals courtesy of Prime Video.
